dispositions.notes: The balance change still licenses the UCT target, but the reread found that the former schematic complement argument named no complex or coefficient group. The repaired proof computes the degree-one UCT for C_1=Ze+Zf -> C_0=Zg, d(e)=2g, with G=Z/2, and its shear automorphism rules out every section.

Balanced Tor still types the UCT quotient correctly, but the old proof inferred nonexistence of a natural splitting from an unspecified changed complement. The repaired Z/2 calculation exhibits a chain automorphism acting trivially on both outer terms and freely on all possible sections.

The corollary reads the segment Tor_1(N,C) -> N tensor A -> N tensor B from the left-variable long exact sequence. Balanced Tor remains natural after the source repair, so image(boundary)=kernel and the stated iff are unaffected.

The field case uses the Kunneth exact sequence and vanishing of every Tor_1 over k. The repaired balance theorem retains the natural Tor bifunctor used by the Kunneth quotient, so the cross product is still a natural isomorphism.

Flatness of each H_p(C) kills Tor_1(H_p(C),H_q(D)) in the Kunneth quotient. That use depends only on the balanced Tor identification, which the current source theorem proves naturally in both variables.

This definition directly identifies H_i(N tensor P) with H_i(Q tensor M) and uses comparison-map coherence on morphisms. Those are precisely the natural balance and resolution-independence conclusions retained by the repaired source and its coherence proposition.
For 0 -> Z --2--> Z, tensoring with Z/2 gives H_1=Z/2, and the UCT quotient identifies it with Tor_1(Z/2,Z/2). The current balanced Tor interface leaves this explicit calculation unchanged.

The displayed zero-differential finite free complexes give alternating ranks 1 and 3, hence tensor-product Euler characteristic 3. Balance affects only the upstream Kunneth justification and still supplies the same Tor terms.
Both two-term complexes have H_0=Z/2 and no positive homology, so the degree-one Kunneth quotient is Tor_1(Z/2,Z/2)=Z/2. The repaired balance theorem preserves that quotient and its typing.

The example computes two one-dimensional homology groups directly and observes that Tor vanishes over a field. The upstream natural balance repair does not alter either calculation or the cross-product map.
The tensor/localization isomorphism N tensor Z[1/2] ~= S^{-1}N proves exactness and hence positive-Tor vanishing. The balanced Tor source still licenses computing in either resolved variable.
The kernel of multiplication by 8 on Z/12 is {0,3,6,9} ~= Z/4. The cyclic Tor theorem reaches the changed source only through the balanced definition, whose natural identification is unchanged.

Tensoring the 12-resolution with Z/18 gives a degree-one kernel generated by 3 of order 6. The source repair changes neither the resolution computation nor the balanced identification of its homology as Tor.
Both cyclic calculations give Z/gcd(4,6)=Z/2, and commutativity supplies the factor swap. The current balance theorem continues to identify the two resolution constructions naturally.
The tensor complex is 0 -> Z/r --m--> Z/r, so its H_1 and H_0 are exactly the stated kernel and cokernel. Balanced Tor only types the upstream UCT correction and remains available unchanged.

The field calculation gives dimension 0, while length-one resolutions over Z and nonzero Tor_1(Z/2,Z/2) give weak dimension 1. The repaired balance theorem still supports the left-right Tor comparison used upstream.
The item only warns that the classical cycle-boundary proof needs flat cycle and boundary modules. The repaired balance interface leaves the Kunneth hypotheses and Tor edge unchanged.
The two multiplication-by-2 complexes have a nonzero degree-one Kunneth correction Tor_1(Z/2,Z/2)=Z/2, so cross product is not always an isomorphism. Balance still validates this correction term.

Natural balanced Tor does not create a canonical Kunneth section, but the former proof supplied no witness. The repaired pair of free complexes has degree-one middle term (Z/2)^2 and a homology-trivial shear that fixes both outer terms while moving every quotient section.

The left-resolved terms N tensor P_q and right-resolved terms Q_p tensor M are not definitionally equal. The repaired source still concludes only a natural homology isomorphism through the tensor double complex, exactly as this refutation requires.

The repaired group-cohomology UCT explicitly separates a natural short exact sequence from a splitting available only after choices. The false statement's target claim of a natural splitting is therefore not introduced by the changed interface.

The homological UCT remains a natural exact sequence with a choice-dependent section. Natural balance of Tor identifies the quotient but does not turn the chosen complement into a natural direct-sum decomposition.

The claimed symmetric bifunctor on two left modules is ill-typed over a noncommutative ring before any resolution is chosen. The repaired balance theorem concerns correctly handed right/left inputs and does not imply the false symmetry.

Balance still gives the correct kernel description, but the former refutation asserted that failure without an example. For R=k[x,y], I=(x,y), M=k, the repaired calculation gives Tor_1^R(R/I,k)=I/I^2~=k^2 while the I-torsion submodule is k.
Q is flat but nonprojective over Z, Z/2 is nonprojective, and Tor_1(Q,Z/2)=0. Natural balance remains valid and does not strengthen vanishing into projectivity.

The item correctly keeps Tor_1 in homological UCT and Ext^1 in cohomological UCT. The repaired balance theorem affects only the well-defined Tor bifunctor, not this variance or correction-term distinction.

The Kunneth quotient is assembled from Tor_1(H_p(C),H_q(D)) using the balanced bifunctor. The current source theorem still supplies the same natural, resolution-independent identification required for that quotient map.
The map factors d_n through B_{n-1}(C); for a tensor cycle its image lies in ker(B_{n-1} tensor G -> Z_{n-1} tensor G)=Tor_1(H_{n-1}C,G). The repaired balance theorem preserves this natural target.

After passage to the fraction field the Tor corrections have rank zero, so finite alternating ranks multiply. The repaired balance theorem does not alter the Kunneth rank identity or the finite-support regrouping.

Over a semisimple ring every module has a degree-zero projective resolution, so positive Tor vanishes (and injectivity gives positive Ext vanishing). The balanced source remains compatible with this calculation in either variable.

Length-one resolutions give both upper bounds and Tor_1(Z/n,Z/n) != 0 gives the weak lower bound. The repaired natural balance theorem retains this Tor group and the left-right weak-dimension comparison.

The signed twist sends [x] times [y] to (-1)^(pq)[y] times [x] and intertwines tensor differentials. Balanced Tor is only an upstream symmetry dependency and its repaired naturality is fully compatible with the twist.

This proposition is the direct coherence consumer of the changed theorem. Its comparison-map squares and homotopy independence use the repaired edge-to-total quasi-isomorphisms exactly, so replacement of either resolution still commutes.

The long exact sequence with projective middle term gives Tor_{i+1}(N,M) ~= Tor_i(N,K), and the right-variable form uses balance. The repaired theorem retains the natural identification needed for that second form.
A torsion-free abelian group is the filtered union of its finitely generated free subgroups, and exact filtered colimits preserve flatness. The balanced Tor repair changes none of this argument.

Universal vanishing of Tor_1(N,M) makes K tensor M -> P tensor M injective for every right-submodule inclusion K -> P, which is exactly flatness. The current balanced Tor interface preserves this criterion.

The right-handed criterion repeats the kernel argument for N tensor K -> N tensor P. The repaired balance theorem still transports the right-resolved construction to the common Tor bifunctor naturally.

Repeated dimension shifting identifies Tor_1(N,K_n) with Tor_{n+1}(N,M), including n=0, and the Tor-one criterion makes K_n flat. The natural balance repair leaves every degree and quantifier unchanged.

Every abelian group has a projective resolution of length at most one, so the complex computing Tor has no degrees >=2. The balanced source still identifies this computation with Tor regardless of the resolved variable.

The theorem's natural short exact sequence uses the balanced Tor quotient supplied through its Tor-map lemma. The repaired source preserves that quotient, while the stated PID, freeness, and finite-diagonal hypotheses remain unchanged.
A degreewise split horseshoe sequence remains exact after tensoring and yields the left-variable long exact sequence. Balanced Tor remains a well-defined natural bifunctor after the source repair.

Resolving the right-variable horseshoe sequence gives the displayed long exact sequence, and the changed source is cited directly to identify it with balanced Tor. Its repaired naturality makes the connecting maps resolution-independent.

Over a PID, flat implies torsion-free by tensoring multiplication by nonzero r, while torsion-free modules are filtered unions of finite free submodules. Balance is only upstream and its repair does not alter either implication.

The homological UCT splitting is constructed from a chosen section onto the free boundary group and expressly carries no naturality claim. Natural balance identifies its Tor quotient but does not remove the choice.

The Kunneth section still depends on chosen cycle-boundary complements. The source repair supplies a natural Tor object and exact sequence, not a canonical section, so the choice-qualified splitting remains licensed.
The kernel of multiplication by m on Z/n is the unique cyclic subgroup of order gcd(m,n), giving Tor_1 ~= Z/gcd(m,n). The balanced identification used upstream is unchanged by the repair.
Tensoring 0 -> Z --n--> Z -> Z/n -> 0 with M computes Tor_1 as ker(n:M->M), including n=1 and zero torsion. The repaired balance theorem preserves this natural calculation.

For commutative R, the Koszul-signed swap of the tensor double complex induces Tor_i(M,N) ~= Tor_i(N,M). The repaired natural balance theorem is exactly the resolution-independence needed in the final step.
The UCT target Tor_1(H_{n-1}C,G) is formed through balanced Tor, while flat cycles and boundaries give the exact sequence. The repaired source preserves the target and its naturality in C and G.

The Tor-vanishing criterion detects each module's flat dimension, and balance interchanges the two module variables without changing degree. The current source theorem retains precisely that natural interchange, so the two suprema still agree.

The generic-point witness uses the residue-field, generic-point, and closed-point consequences of the affine structure sheaf, not the former basis-extension proof. The repaired construction retains the same stalks and distinguished-open sections, so the domain, quotient, and k-algebra-kernel argument is unchanged.

The counterexample compares the one-point spectra of k and its dual numbers and separates them by reducedness. The repaired structure-sheaf construction keeps the same coordinate rings and global sections, so the homeomorphism and nonisomorphism conclusions remain valid.

The corollary uses the affine anti-equivalence and its global-sections quasi-inverse. The repaired sheaf still has Gamma(Spec A,O)=A and the same maps on distinguished opens, so both directions of the isomorphism criterion are unchanged.

Quasi-compactness is a property of the underlying spectrum: an affine presentation identifies X with Spec A and Spec A=D(1). The repaired sheaf interface changes neither that topology nor the basic-open compactness argument, including A=0.

The corollary needs only the retained stalk identification O_p=A_p and the fact that A_p is local. The germ-family extension proves the same stalk calculation, so every stalk still has maximal ideal pA_p.

The definition quantifies over locally ringed spaces already isomorphic to a constructed affine spectrum. The repaired theorem supplies that same locally ringed spectrum and the same global-section coordinate ring; it adds no condition to the object-level definition.
Closedness is topological, and closed points of Spec A remain exactly maximal ideals. Neither the arbitrary-cover repair nor the germ-family extension changes the underlying prime spectrum.

The dual-numbers scheme is the affine spectrum of k[epsilon]/(epsilon^2). The repaired construction exists for this ring, retains its localization sections, and leaves the nonzero square-zero class and nonreduced conclusion unchanged.

The identification Hom_Sch(Spec R,Spec A)=Hom_CRing(A,R) uses the retained affine anti-equivalence. The repaired structure sheaf has the same global and localized sections, so covariance in R and the displayed natural bijection are unchanged.
The equality closure({p})=V(p) concerns only the unchanged Zariski topology. The structure-sheaf repair therefore has no effect on the definition or on a prime being generic for V(p).

The equivalence between a nonzero domain coordinate ring and a nonempty reduced irreducible affine spectrum uses the unchanged global ring and prime-spectrum topology. The zero-ring exclusion and both directions remain intact.

A ring map still induces contraction on primes and the same localization maps A_f to B_phi(f). Those maps are exactly the basis data preserved by the repaired sheaf extension, so the ringed-space morphism is unchanged.

For nilpotent I, Spec(A/I) to Spec A remains a homeomorphism on primes while the global-section map can remove nilpotents. The repaired sheaf keeps both the quotient-induced localization maps and Gamma(Spec A,O)=A.

Reducedness is read from any affine coordinate ring, and presentation independence follows from the retained reflection of affine-scheme isomorphisms by global sections. The repair changes neither coordinate rings nor their nilradicals.

The repaired structure sheaf has the same stalk A_p at p, hence the same maximal ideal pA_p and residue field A_p/pA_p isomorphic to Frac(A/p). The localization and zero-boundary conventions are unchanged.
The example uses the retained locally ringed-space identification Spec(k[t]_t)=D(t) and the algebraic equality k[t]_t=k[t,t^{-1}]. The repaired sheaf agrees with the same localization data on D(t).

The explicit unit calculation still gives Nil(k[epsilon]/epsilon^2)=(epsilon), one prime, residue field k, and a nonzero square-zero element. The repaired affine sheaf retains the same stalk and coordinate ring.

The example is the relative polynomial universal-property bijection Hom_k-Alg(k[t],R)=R. The affine anti-equivalence used to interpret it as scheme-valued points remains valid with the repaired sheaf.
A field still has the sole prime (0); the repaired sheaf gives stalk k_(0)=k and global sections k. Thus the one-point, local-ring, residue-field, and global-ring assertions all remain valid.
The classification of primes of Z and the closure calculations are topological and algebraic. The changed sheaf interfaces do not affect (0) being generic or the maximal ideals (p) being closed.

Prime ideals of A times B still split into the two clopen families, and localization on each family is A_p or B_q. The repaired extension preserves those localizations, so the locally ringed disjoint-union isomorphism remains valid.

The zero ring has no proper prime ideals, and the repaired theorem explicitly covers its empty spectrum. Its empty germ family is the unique global section, agreeing with the zero ring as the basic-open calculation requires.
The proof transfers compactness across the unchanged homeomorphism Spec(A_f)=D(f). The sheaf repair does not alter the topology and explicitly retains the zero-localization and empty-open boundary.

The closed-point characterization uses maximal ideals and the finite-type algebraic-closed-field theorem. Both concern the unchanged prime topology and coordinate ring, so the exact kernel classification and warning about nonclosed points remain valid.

The underlying localization homeomorphism is unchanged, and on every D(g) inside D(f) the repaired sheaf still identifies sections with (A_f)_(g/1)=A_g compatibly with restrictions. Hence the open locally ringed subspace claim remains typed.
The repaired sheaf produces the same stalk map A_p to B_q induced by localization. Its inverse image of qB_q is still pA_p, so the localness proof and all quantifiers are unchanged.

The remark uses the unchanged contravariant affine correspondence, residue fields, and distinction among generic, closed, and ground-field-valued points. The repaired sheaf introduces no contrary identification.

The repaired sheaf retains Gamma(Spec A,O)=A, the localization maps on basic opens, and local stalk maps. These are exactly the inputs proving the natural Hom bijection and the global-sections quasi-inverse.

Yoneda still turns a natural isomorphism of the representable affine functors into mutually inverse scheme morphisms. The repaired affine anti-equivalence preserves the representing objects and their Hom functors.
The repaired structure sheaf agrees with the localization basis on D(1)=Spec A, so Gamma(Spec A,O)=A_1=A. The theorem's explicit A=0 case is also covered by the empty germ-family construction.

Agreement of the repaired sheaf with the basis assignment gives Gamma(D(f),O)=A_f and the canonical restriction A_f to A_g exactly as stated. Empty D(f) still corresponds to the zero localization and its unique section.

Sobriety follows from the unchanged correspondence between irreducible closed subsets and prime ideals. Its own Choice hypothesis remains explicit, and the structure-sheaf repair has no effect on existence or uniqueness of generic points.
The repaired sheaf has sections A_f on the cofinal distinguished neighborhoods of p. Their colimit is still A_p, so the canonical stalk isomorphism is unchanged.

The former consumer of the basis lemma was repaired in cycle 4: it now assumes Choice, constructs locally representable germ families on every open, proves sheafness and basis agreement, and proves uniqueness through the prescribed basis identifications, including the empty spectrum. Its current proof directly uses the strengthened arbitrary-cover basis lemma.
